Brentford aim for 'special things' after ending 89-year Old Trafford wait

"Slightly surreal."

That is how Brentford manager Keith Andrews summed up the club's first win at Manchester United in 89 years.

The Bees may have been waiting nearly nine decades to win at Old Trafford, but ended that run in style by thrashing Mauricio Pochettino's strugglers 4-0 on Saturday.

Brentford's last win at United before this weekend was in February 1937 - the longest any side has gone between victories against the Red Devils, surpassing Bristol City's 69-year wait between 1909 and 1978.

Granted, Brentford had only played eight games on United's turf since then, given the clubs' contrasting fortunes.

But the emphatic way in which they ended that streak is surely cause for celebration for a club who just 12 years ago were competing in League One.

"Slightly surreal if I am honest," Brentford boss Andrews told BBC Match of the Day.

"We have been keen to enjoy the journey. We want to be really ambitious but [with a] level of humility. I think we can achieve special things because I think it is a special group."

Brentford have cemented their status as an established Premier League club but "special things" suggests Andrews sees his side going even further.

After a second consecutive 4-0 win, having thrashed Everton by the same score on Monday, the Bees are now fifth in the league and with European football in their sights.

Andrews surpassing expectation

Andrews' appointment at Brentford in 2025 divided opinion after the departure of Thomas Frank, who had rightly earned the adoration of the fans having led them to the top flight.

While some fans trusted the judgement of the board, others suggested hiring someone who had never been a first-team manager before showed a lack of ambition.

There can now be little debate around Andrews' position.

The Irishman was handed a new contract in February - just eight months into the job - and after finishing 10th last season, he has his sights set on more this campaign.

"I haven't been doing this for very long, but it has been a special week," the 46-year-old told Sky Sports after the win at Old Trafford.

"I thought we were well worthy of getting the three points. We could have been more clinical and that was the message at half-time.

"Could we take the handbrake off more? Could we go for it? I fancy us all the time when we're in those areas.

"Twelve games in and we're in a good groove. We feel we do a lot of things right."

The former midfielder's strategy to go for more rather than defend their 2-0 half-time lead speaks volumes for how he views the potential in his side - and it ultimately paid off as they further punished United's frailties.

When asked about making history at United, Andrews referenced legendary Bees boss Harry Curtis - Brentford's longest-serving and most successful manager to date.

"First one in the Premier League and first win since Harry Curtis was manager," he said.

"They were special days for Brentford going back a long time. Now it is nice to be part of the current journey."

Bees set sights on Europe

Since promotion to the top flight in 2021, the closest Brentford have come to relegation was when they finished 16th under Frank in 2023-24.

They have taken to life in the Premier League with relative ease - a remarkable achievement given they were competing in League Two less than 20 years ago.

Forward Callum Wilson who scored his first top-flight goals for Brentford with a double against United - in the absence of injured striker Igor Thiago - said the club are aiming high.

"It is a smaller club that does everything to the maximum of their abilities," he said.

"Everyone on the inside feels they belong at this level. The club's next step in their transition is to win a trophy or step up to Europe.

"Back-to-back 4-0s, which is nice, but it comes down to the hard work that everyone puts in behind the scenes.

"It was a nice moment and everyone got to celebrate at the end."

Following victory over the Toffees last week Andrews called for critics of his side to "get real", suggesting expectation levels had spiralled considering their journey.

"The expectation levels, I think, at this club have changed and maybe the outside world have changed a little bit," he said.

"Regardless of the performance or the result... there's still a little bit swirling in the air - we're a little bit unhappy or should they be doing a little bit better?

"Maybe people need to get a little bit real.

"I'm really happy with our group. I'm really happy with our football club and long may that continue."

Selby & Williams win on day one of UK Championship

Defending champion Mark Selby moved into the last 16 of the UK Championship with a comfortable 6-2 win over Matthew Selt, while Mark Williams defeated Stephen Maguire 6-5 in a see-saw affair at York Barbican.

Selt had led 2-1 but Selby, who made the two highest breaks of the contest with an 87 and a 56, then took control reeling off five consecutive frames to advance.

While both players were far from their best, Selby's ability to score more heavily than his opponent ultimately told in an error-strewn affair.

"It was not great but if you get through you can only improve. We sort of both cancelled each other out a bit," Selby told BBC Sport.

"Towards the end we both missed a few and it was a comedy of errors and it was a case of just getting over the line. I think 6-2 is a flattering scoreline - it could have been a lot closer than that."

Selby will now face Chang Bingyu or Zhou Yuelong, who play later on Saturday evening.

On the opposite side of the arena, Scotland's Maguire - the winner in 2004 and also a finalist in 2007 and 2019 - had the better of things early on against Williams and took a 3-1 advantage into the mid-session interval.

However, the Welshman, whose second UK title was back in 2002, responded with breaks of 51, a superb century and a 56 as he took the next four frames.

And while Maguire rallied to win the next two, Williams got in early in the 11th and final frame and a run of 53 helped him build a 57-point advantage before his opponent conceded after failing to get position on the black.

Williams will take on England's Kyren Wilson or China's Fan Zhengyi next.

item.title: Cameron Mason on his breakthrough win and upcoming home World Cup: 'If it’s not muddy I’ll be pretty angry'
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Cameron Mason is having a very good winter, and it's just getting started.

The now-26-year-old Scot has been – as they say – there or thereabouts for a handful of seasons, regularly featuring in top fives and top 10s, and dominating the British National Championships since 2023. Steadily climbing through the ranks, Mason surged onto his first elite podiums a handful of times during the 2023-24 season, took his first World Cup top five at Hulst in late 2024, then powered onto the podium at World Cup Flamanville last year, gaining in consistency all the while. Since starting his 2026-27 season at HG Cross Dendermonde in mid-October, Mason had only finished outside the top six once before taking the biggest win of his career at a very muddy Superprestige Niel on 11th November.

Mason is a rider who has always exuded a certain amount of self-assurance, but he's appeared more confident than ever so far this winter. And the timing could not be any better as the cyclocross world, and Mason's fans at home, look forward to a brand-new World Cup round in Glasgow on Sunday 13th December.

We spoke to Mason a few days before the World Cup got underway with round one in Ostrava, Czech Republic (where Mason would finish a brilliant fourth in thoroughly wintery conditions), to talk all things cyclocross, including his journey through the sport, his loyalty to home roads, his breakthrough win at Niel, and the buildup to his home World Cup in a few weeks' time.

Escape Collective: Can you tell me a bit about where you’re from and how you got into cyclocross?

Cameron Mason: I’m from Scotland, I was born in Livingston, grew up in Linlithgow [in West Lothian, about 30 km west of the capital], and now live in Edinburgh. My job is a professional cyclocross racer, has been since I left school, but in the last few years, it’s more serious and it’s definitely my full-time job.

I used to race all types of bikes when I was little: mountain bikes, road bikes, cyclocross bikes, discovering all the different disciplines. I tried pretty much everything, but I always leant more towards the off-road stuff. I used to race Scottish cross-country mountain bike in the summer, then the Scottish cyclocross races in the winter, and that just gave me some great fun things to do at the weekend in between school, and then that got more serious over the years.

item.title: All Blacks bite back in Nations Championship dismantling of England
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source. (Clean-up failed for this item, so the body is a truncated excerpt of the original.)

Why it is here: Clear reporting and useful vocabulary.

Nations Championship - England 8-26 New Zealand: All Blacks bite back in dismantling of Steve Borthwick's side a week on from record loss

Wallace Sititi, Cam Roigard score tries, while Richie Mo'unga kicks 16 points as New Zealand comprehensively defeat England at Allianz Stadium Twickenham, a week on from suffering record 25-point defeat to same opposition at same venue; England see Alex Coles, Henry Pollock sin-binned

By Michael Cantillon at Allianz Stadium Twickenham

Last Updated: 28/11/26 6:38pm

New Zealand bounced back from their record 25-point defeat to England to stun Steve Borthwick's charges a week on with a 26-8 Nations Championship victory at Allianz Stadium Twickenham.

England actually scored the opening points via a long-range Henry Slade penalty in the third minute, but did not trouble the scoreboard again in torrential Twickenham rain until the 75th minute - hooker Jamie George scoring a maul try.

The All Blacks scored tries in either half through No 8 Wallace Sititi and scrum-half Cam Roigard - the latter a stunning finish in the corner - as Dave Rennie's side produced a thorough dismantling of the hosts.

Fly-half Richie Mo'unga also kicked superbly for the visitors, landing both conversions and four penalties against an ill-disciplined England, who were shown yellow cards to lock Alex Coles (high tackle) and replacement back-row Henry Pollock (offside, repeat team penalties).

- As it happened: Stunned England beaten heavily by All Blacks in rematch

- Scratchy Ireland still prove too strong for Australia at Twickenham

- Erasmus set for France watchalong as SA coaches deny contact during Ireland loss

- Nations Championship: Results, schedule as France vs South Africa in final

England 8-26 New Zealand - Score summary

England - Tries: George (75). Pens: Slade (3).

New Zealand - Tries: Sititi (17), Roigard (46). Cons: Mo'unga (18,47). Pens: Mo'unga (41,43,54,66).

New Zealand lock Scott Barrett was also shown yellow late on for repeat team penalties, but by then the All Blacks were home and hosed as far as the result was concerned against a shocked England.

As if to sum up England's miserable day, Marcus Smith near comically ended up on his backside while attempting the straightforward conversion for George's late try, leaving England stuck in single digits for points for the first time in over three years (August 2023).

Story of the match

Less than a minute into the contest, New Zealand's starting scrum-half Cortez Ratima was penalised for failing to release in a jackal attempt on halfway, with England's Slade stepping up to notch three points off the tee from distance.

Two big chances then came and went for the hosts. First, a maul collapse handed England a lineout deep in the 22, only for Anton Segner to rise and steal it, before Coles then spilled the ball on the run within the 22 as a try looked likely.

The All Blacks made England pay for such profligacy, with Rieko Ioane and Ratima breaks paving the way for Sititi to finish strongly from close range in the 17th minute.

Mo'unga converted for the full haul, with England then suffering two further pointless visits to the New Zealand 22 - the second particularly costly as Slade kicked dead with a penalty kick from hand.

England were then reduced to 14 six minutes from half-time with Coles sin-binned for a head-on-head tackle on opposite number Fabian Holland.

Despite missing out via a five-metre lineout maul, New Zealand would stretch their lead to seven before the break, as Mo'unga struck over after Tommy Freeman had cheaply kicked the ball away to deny the visitors the chance to take a Roigard 50:22 quickly.

The second half started poorly for England from the off as they knocked on the restart, and though Freddie Steward produced a crunching tackle on Damian McKenzie, a breakdown penalty saw Mo'unga stretch the lead to 10 points.

Coles returned from his sin-bin shortly after to restore England to the full complement, but within moments the All Blacks blew out the score-board through Roigard's fabulous try after Ollie Chessum gave away a maul penalty.

Mo'unga added the difficult extras too for a 17-point lead, and though Borthwick made a raft of changes to attempt to alter things, Mo'unga added more points to the total with another penalty soon after as England kept infringing.

A remarkable piece of Scott Barrett defence held up Ben Curry to end a period of huge England pressure, while two very poor kicks out of hand followed from Marcus Smith, both too long and marked by New Zealand under little pressure, with the crowd booing in reply.

Instead, New Zealand would score again through the boot of Mo'unga next after the hosts were again reduced to 14 with Pollock shown yellow into the final quarter.

George added a try for England in what remained, but it was of scant consolation, while Slade knocked on in the corner as they sought a second in the final few moments.

Itoje admits England not 'finished article' after sobering defeat - 'Not good enough'

England captain Maro Itoje told ITV:

"We just weren't good enough today, no excuses. As individuals, as a collective, we weren't good enough and the result reflected that.

"A lot of these things [differences in performance] come down to accuracy and execution. We put pressure on ourselves, gave away territory and put ourselves in trouble.

"We've done a lot of good stuff in this campaign. We were flying in the first three games, today was a bit trickier.

"We're not the finished article, we've always known that. We need to take our medicine today and come back stronger for the Six Nations."

Borthwick: New Zealand handled conditions better than we did

England head coach Steve Borthwick told ITV:

"Full credit to New Zealand. The conditions were difficult and they played them better than we did.

"They were dominant in terms of territory, and that gave them scoring chances. They executed the kicking game much better than we did, we need to look very closely at that.…

Report and free match highlights as Leif Davis hits second-half equaliser for Ipswich who fell behind twice; Alysson and Joao Gomes had put Aston Villa in front

Saturday 28 November 2026 19:35, UK

Ipswich came from behind twice to pick up a 2-2 draw with Aston Villa, who extended their run of unbeaten Premier League games to eight.

There was a snap and purpose about Aston Villa in the early stages. Boubacar Kamara had already sliced a great opening wide before Alysson scampered through following a Johan Manzambi pass to send the visitors ahead.

Ipswich rallied though and within two minutes were level as Emersonn was given the freedom of the Villa box to twist and fire home.

Villa regained control though with Manzambi pulling the strings. The second goal came from a corner as Joao Gomes produced an epic acrobatic finish to silence Portman Road.

Ipswich didn't carry too much of a threat but a moment of inspiration down the left from Julio Enciso was finished with a clever header by Leif Davis.

Villa remain unbeaten in their last eight games - the longest current unbeaten run in the Premier League - although they have drawn their last four.

Ipswich are now six games without a win in the Premier League - only Man Utd (10) are on a longer current run without a victory.
